bugs.creator: ikrylov
bugs.summary: strptime() parses shortest prefix of localised month name

comments.text:
In some locales, `strptime()` will misunderstand month names if some of them are prefixes of others:

```
# sudo apt install locales-all,
#  or add "vi_VN UTF-8" to /etc/locale.gen and run locale-gen
Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "vi_VN")
d <- as.Date('2000-11-01')
f <- '%Y %d %b'
d |> strftime(f) |> strptime(f)
# [1] "2000-01-01 UTC"
```

This happens because in the vi_VN locale, month names are formatted as "Tháng 1" ... "Tháng 12" (`%B`) or "Thg 1" ... "Thg 12" (`%b`) and R's own internal `strptime()` [parses them as](https://svn.r-project.org/browse/R/trunk/src/main/Rstrptime.h?op=blame&rev=83234#l297):

```
if (w_match_string (w_weekday_name[cnt], rp)) break;
// ...
if (w_match_string (w_ab_weekday_name[cnt], rp)) break;
```

...i.e., as soon as R sees "Thg 1", the match is successful. This leads to problems with the `%b` format in the following locales:

* bo_CN
* bo_IN
* dz_BT
* km_KH
* tok
* shn_MM (where July ("လၼသပး") is a prefix of November ("လၼသပးသင"))
* vi_VN
comments.creator: ikrylov

comments.text:
Tangentially related: when playing around with this behavior a bit, I also noticed the following confusing error:


```
Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "zh_CN")
Sys.getlocale()
# [1] "LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8;LC_NUMERIC=C;LC_TIME=zh_CN;LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8;LC_MONETARY=en_US.UTF-8;LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8;LC_PAPER=en_US.UTF-8;LC_NAME=C;LC_ADDRESS=C;LC_TELEPHONE=C;LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8;LC_IDENTIFICATION=C"

roundtrip = \() strptime(strftime(as.Date('2000-11-01'), '%Y %d %b'), '%Y %d %b')

roundtrip()
# Error in strptime(strftime(as.Date("2000-11-01"), "%Y %d %b"), "%Y %d %b") : 
#   input string is too long

# c.f.
strftime(as.Date("2000-11-01"), "%Y %d %b")
# [1] "2000 01 11\xd4\xc2"
```

It's unusual to have this particular locale setting; more typical would be:

```
Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "zh_CN")
roundtrip()
# [1] "2000-11-01 UTC"
```

And this works too:

```
Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "zh_CN.utf8")
roundtrip()
# [1] "2000-11-01 UTC"
```

So it's because of a mismatch in the inferred encoding under `zh_CN` (GB2312).

comments.text:
Created attachment 3771
Switch order of checking mbcstowcs failure

For my previous comment, the attached patch gives a friendlier error by checking for conversion failure first:

```
Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "zh_CN")
Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "zh_CN.utf8")
strptime(strftime(as.Date('2000-11-01'), '%Y %d %b'), '%Y %d %b')
# Error in strptime(strftime(as.Date("2000-11-01"), "%Y %d %b"), "%Y %d %b") : 
#   invalid multibyte input string
```

This is a more conservative patch, I think we can also consolidate to just one call to `mbcstowcs()` because `wbuf` has fixed size, i.e., the `mbcstowcs(NULL, buf, 0)` call is not needed, but I'm not 100% confident here.
